objective:
Build the deterministic TAG RESOLVER and DECISION POLICY in core-domain for the subject+action tagging redesign. Background: the AI now only extracts words (TG1.2: core-domain `extraction` package -- ExtractionCandidate(operation, subject, action, activityState, temporalExpression, durationExpression), all UNTRUSTED). Every logged entry will carry a SUBJECT tag (what it was done to: 'hot tub') and an ACTION tag (what was done: 'change filter'). This task turns extracted words into tag decisions with plain, PC-testable program logic: normalize -> exact name -> alias -> close match, then decide AUTO_SAVE (log silently) / CONFIRM (quick 'did you mean X?' card, nothing saved silently) / NEEDS_REVIEW (nothing logged). It must work from an EMPTY catalog (new tags allowed) while always preferring an existing close tag over creating a near-duplicate. No database, no app wiring, no AI, no scoring (TG1.4).

DECISIONS ALREADY MADE (follow them):
(1) New package com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.domain.tagging (core-domain main), pure Kotlin, no I/O, no clock, no logging, deterministic, KDoc on every public type/function/constant in the style of naming/NameNormalizer.kt and validation/InterpretationValidator.kt. Suggested files (you may split/merge sensibly): TagCatalog.kt, TagNormalizer.kt, TagResolver.kt, TagDecisionPolicy.kt.
(2) Catalog input types: enum TagKind { SUBJECT, ACTION }; data class KnownTag(id: String, kind: TagKind, displayName: String, aliases: List<String>); data class KnownPair(subjectId: String, actionId: String) (a known subject+action combination, i.e. today's 'activity'); data class TagCatalog(subjects: List<KnownTag>, actions: List<KnownTag>, pairs: List<KnownPair>) with init checks (kinds match their list; ids unique per kind; pair ids resolve) and TagCatalog.EMPTY.
(3) TagNormalizer (object):
   - cleanName(words): String? -- the display form of user words for a NEW tag: NameNormalizer-style whitespace collapse and trim of surrounding punctuation, strip leading determiners/possessives (the, a, an, my, our, your, his, her, their, its, all, all the, some), keep the user's casing and spelling otherwise ('the Wi-Fi' -> 'Wi-Fi', 'all the dishes' -> 'dishes'); null when nothing is left.
   - key(words): String -- the comparison key: lowercase (Locale.ROOT), determiners/possessives stripped as above, hyphens/apostrophes/other punctuation removed, each token naively singularized (documented, conservative rules, e.g. -ies->-y, -ses/-xes/-ches/-shes drop -es, trailing -s dropped when the token is longer than 3 letters and not ending in -ss/-us/-is), then tokens joined with NO separator so 'Wi-Fi' == 'WiFi' == 'wifi' and 'lawn mower' == 'lawnmower'. Also expose tokens(words): List<String> (the singularized tokens before joining). Idempotent; tests for each rule.
(4) TagResolver.resolve(words: String?, kind: TagKind, catalog: TagCatalog): TagResolution, compared only against tags of the same kind. sealed TagResolution: Empty (no usable words); Exact(tag: KnownTag, via: TagMatchVia { NAME, ALIAS }); Near(newName: String, candidates: List<KnownTag>) (close to one or more existing tags -- candidates ranked closest first, ties by displayName then id, so output is deterministic); New(name: String) (nothing close). Order: key(words) equals key(displayName) -> Exact NAME; equals key(alias) -> Exact ALIAS; otherwise close-match; otherwise New. CLOSE-MATCH RULES (named constants, documented, tuned so the oracle test in (7) passes):
   a) Spelling: optimal-string-alignment (Damerau) edit distance between keys <= 1 when the shorter key has >= 5 characters, <= 2 when >= 9; never for keys shorter than 5 (so 'wash' is not near 'walk' or 'wax').
   b) Token overlap for SUBJECTS: any shared token of >= 3 letters makes it near ('lawn mower' ~ 'lawn'; 'dryer lint trap' ~ 'dryer vent').
   c) Token overlap for ACTIONS: near only when they share a token OTHER than each phrase's first token (the verb) -- 'change oil' is NOT near 'change filter' and 'replace batteries' is NOT near 'replace filter', but 'replace filter' IS near 'change filter'.
   No synonym dictionary in this task (grass/lawn, HVAC/furnace stay unmatched; TG1.4 measures that). Near never auto-saves.
(5) TagDecisionPolicy.decide(extraction: ExtractionCandidate, catalog: TagCatalog): TagDecision with data class TagDecision(outcome: TagDecisionOutcome, subject: TagResolution, action: TagResolution, subjectInferred: Boolean, reasons: Set<TagDecisionReason>) and enum TagDecisionOutcome { AUTO_SAVE, CONFIRM, NEEDS_REVIEW }. Rules, in this order:
   - operation != LOG_ACTIVITY -> NEEDS_REVIEW (reason NOT_A_LOG). (Questions are handled by a later stage.)
   - action Empty -> NEEDS_REVIEW (ACTION_MISSING).
   - VAGUE action -> NEEDS_REVIEW (VAGUE_ACTION): the action's first token (after key-style lowercasing, before singularizing) is in a small documented set of content-free verbs: do, did, done, doing, handle, handled, work, worked, fix, fixed, deal, dealt, take care, sort, sorted -- but only when the action has no further object word, OR the phrase is one of 'work on', 'deal with', 'take care of', 'sort out'. ('fix' alone is vague; 'fix fence' as an action is not.)
   - FILLER: subject or action words contain a whole-word filler (thing, things, stuff) -> NEEDS_REVIEW (FILLER_WORDS).
   - a New name failing new-tag rules -> NEEDS_REVIEW (NEW_NAME_REJECTED): reuse NewActivityNameCheck where its rules fit tags (length, no meaningful text, digits only, first-person opener, time words, completion words, filler) -- call it, do not copy it; do not change NewActivityNameCheck.
   - subject Empty: if the action is Exact and exactly ONE KnownPair has that action, infer that pair's subject (subject becomes Exact(tag, via NAME), subjectInferred = true). Otherwise NEEDS_REVIEW (SUBJECT_MISSING).
   - any Near (subject or action) -> CONFIRM (SUBJECT_NEAR_EXISTING / ACTION_NEAR_EXISTING).
   - otherwise (each tag Exact or New, nothing near) -> AUTO_SAVE with no reasons.
   The model's confidence is not consulted (the extraction has none). Time wording, duration and state are NOT judged here (time resolution stays TemporalResolver's job, ADR-028/TM1); document this in KDoc. reasons is empty exactly when outcome is AUTO_SAVE. TagDecisionReason constant names may later be persisted: document that renaming is a data change.
(6) core-domain unit tests (src/test/.../core/domain/tagging/): TagNormalizerTest (each rule, idempotence, Wi-Fi/WiFi/wifi, lawn mower/lawnmower, dishes/dish, dogs/dog, batteries/battery, glass/grass not mangled, possessive/determiner stripping, cleanName keeps casing), TagResolverTest (empty catalog -> New; Exact by name and alias; kind isolation; each close rule incl. the negative cases in (4); deterministic candidate ranking; blank/null -> Empty), TagCatalogTest (init checks), TagDecisionPolicyTest (every rule and its ordering, pair inference incl. 0 or 2+ pairs -> no inference, empty-catalog AUTO_SAVE, reasons empty iff AUTO_SAVE, speech-slip shapes such as subject 'James Durango' -> New, never Exact to an unrelated tag).
(7) ORACLE TEST in core-testing (src/test/.../core/testing/corpus/TagPolicyOracleTest.kt): for the tag-corpus cases listed below, feed the policy a HAND-WRITTEN ideal extraction (operation LOG_ACTIVITY, the subject/action words given here, nulls elsewhere) against the case's fixture converted to a TagCatalog (write a small converter TagCorpusCatalogs.toTagCatalog(fixture) in core-testing main, package ...core.testing.corpus), and assert: outcome mapped to TagOutcome is in case.expected.acceptableOutcomes; when AUTO_SAVE, each Exact tag id is acceptable for that side (existingId/allowedExistingIds, or the expected subject is mayBeEmpty), each New name matches acceptableNewNames case-insensitively after trim, no AUTO_SAVE resolves to a mustNotMatch id, and a New tag is never produced where the expected side has existingId (that would be a silent duplicate). If a case genuinely cannot pass without breaking a rule above, do NOT weaken the rule silently and do NOT edit tag-corpus.json: list it in an explicit, commented KNOWN_POLICY_GAPS set in the test (asserted to be exactly the failing set) and explain each in your report. Expected: none, except possibly p-edge-no-edge-catalog-finished-edging-style subject inference, which is not in the table.
(8) Docs: add ADR-039 to docs/DECISIONS.md (same format as ADR-038): 'Tag decisions are deterministic: exact/alias/close match, then save / confirm / review' -- amends ADR-027 FOR THE TAG PATH ONLY (InterpretationValidator and the v3 path are unchanged until Stage 3): model confidence is not a gate; AUTO_SAVE when each tag is exact or new-with-nothing-close and the words are clean; any close-but-not-exact -> CONFIRM; missing/vague/filler -> NEEDS_REVIEW; pair inference of an omitted subject; normalization and close-match rules with their thresholds as provisional, to be tuned on recordings in TG1.4. Add a short paragraph to docs/SEMANTIC_CORPUS.md section 12 noting the oracle test exists and what it does (ideal extraction, not a model).

RULES: no capture text in any log or failure message (AGENTS.md #11). Do not modify InterpretationValidator, NameNormalizer, NewActivityNameCheck, the extraction/interpretation packages, tag-corpus.json, corpus.json, recordings, or any existing test. No Room/repository/app changes.
non_goals: No persistence, Room tables, repository or migration (Stage 2).
No wiring into the capture orchestrator, phone or watch (Stage 3).
No change to InterpretationValidator or the v3 confidence policy.
No replay of recordings, scoring, report or gate (TG1.4).
No synonym dictionary or AI call in resolution.
acceptance_criteria: core-domain has a `tagging` package with TagCatalog/KnownTag/KnownPair/TagKind, TagNormalizer (cleanName, key, tokens), TagResolver (Empty/Exact NAME|ALIAS/Near/New) and TagDecisionPolicy (AUTO_SAVE/CONFIRM/NEEDS_REVIEW with reasons), pure and deterministic, fully KDoc'd, with thresholds as named constants.

Normalization merges Wi-Fi/WiFi/wifi, lawn mower/lawnmower and simple plurals, strips determiners/possessives, and is idempotent; close-match follows rules 4a-4c including the negative cases (wash/walk/wax not near; change oil not near change filter; replace batteries not near replace filter; lawn mower near lawn).

The policy follows rule order in (5): NOT_A_LOG, ACTION_MISSING, VAGUE_ACTION, FILLER_WORDS, NEW_NAME_REJECTED, pair inference / SUBJECT_MISSING, NEAR -> CONFIRM, else AUTO_SAVE; reasons empty iff AUTO_SAVE; model confidence is never consulted; works from an empty catalog.

TagPolicyOracleTest runs the 49 listed cases with hand-written ideal extractions against their fixtures and passes: every outcome acceptable, no silent duplicate of an expected existing tag, no AUTO_SAVE to a mustNotMatch tag, acceptable new names; any KNOWN_POLICY_GAPS are explicit, asserted and explained.
ADR-039 records the tag decision policy as amending ADR-027 for the tag path only; SEMANTIC_CORPUS.md section 12 mentions the oracle test.
No change to InterpretationValidator, naming, extraction or interpretation packages, corpus/tag-corpus/recordings, or any existing test; all core-domain and core-testing tests pass.
